sources.title: Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security (Executive Order 14352)

status_summary: No Entity List designation of WeChat, Tencent, ByteDance or TikTok was found: Federal Register API queries of BIS documents since 2025-01-20 for each name returned no results. Executive Order 14352, signed 2025-09-25, instead found that a framework creating a U.S. TikTok joint venture, majority-owned by U.S. persons with ByteDance and affiliates below 20 percent, was a qualified divestiture under the 2024 divest-or-ban law. The joint venture closed on 2026-01-22, with ByteDance keeping nearly 20 percent and licensing its algorithm, and the app continues to operate. This route keeps the app running, the opposite of the outcome the Mandate sought.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14352 determined that a TikTok U.S. joint venture framework, with ByteDance and affiliates holding less than 20 percent, was a qualified divestiture under the 2024 divest-or-ban law (published 2025-09-30).

TikTok closed a deal placing its U.S. operations in a joint venture controlled by American investors; ByteDance keeps nearly 20 percent and licenses its algorithm to the venture (reported 2026-01-23).

title: Designate WeChat and TikTok owners on the Entity List to disable the apps
uncertainties: The Federal Register API checks are term searches of BIS documents (TikTok, WeChat, and a combined query including ByteDance and Tencent), not a review of every Entity List rule; a listing of a related subsidiary under another name would not appear. Axios gives the closing day as a Thursday, which is 2026-01-22; joint venture terms come from news reports, not transaction documents. Neither Axios nor the order mentions the Entity List. Related records c00-13 and c28-03 track TikTok from other chapters.
